subject: Elastic capacity design and burst ops for Stargazer Labs
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver@stargazerlabs.com>

Subject: Dedicated sizing + burst strategy questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — liked how the runtime handled short bursts during our pilot. Before we get too deep on procurement, our infra/ops team has a few open questions about how dedicated capacity can handle our weekly demo spikes and product launch events. High level:

- Typical baseline: 4 sustained A100-equivalent GPUs (in steady-state) for model A (vicuna-13B variant).
- Peak patterns: ~2x–3x baseline during scheduled demos (3 hours, twice a week) and occasional ad-hoc surges during customer webinars (~6x for ~30–90 minutes).
- Need: predictable SLOs for latency (<450ms p95) during demos, and a predictable billing model for burst usage that doesn't explode our forecast.

Questions:
1) How do you recommend structuring a reserved slab vs. burst pool for this profile?
2) What are the preemption policies for burst nodes (will we see sudden evictions during a demo)?
3) Can we get a sample mutual action plan (timeline + approvals) to include legal/procurement?

I can share a spreadsheet with our actual weekly traces if that helps — attaching a short summary.

Thanks,
Oliver Park
Head of Infrastructure, Stargazer Labs

Hi Oliver — thanks for the detail and the spreadsheet, looks very helpful. Pasting the quick proposal below so your procurement and infra teams have something concrete to react to. Marcus and Ben are looped in for technical ops and SRE considerations.

Proposed approach (dedicated + elastic burst):
- Reserved slab: 4 A100-equivalent GPUs pinned to your account for steady-state; reserved capacity keeps baseline latency predictable and avoids cold starts.
- Elastic burst pool: preemptible/burst nodes that can scale up to an additional 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (total peak = 12) for short windows. These nodes are priced at a premium hourly burst rate but billed only while serving.
- Headroom & autoscale policy: maintain a 20% headroom above typical demo peak during scheduled windows (we can hard-cap for cost predictability). Autoscale will:
  * Warm-up: spin additional nodes with a 60s provision window (optimistic for hot-cache; see Marcus notes)
  * Eviction order: burst nodes are preemptible; on capacity pressure we drain burst nodes first, then fall back to a smaller model variant (vicuna-7B) if target latency is at risk.

SLOs and fallbacks:
- Target p95 latency: <450ms on reserved+burst during scheduled demos; if burst pool is exhausted, automatic model-fallback preserves p99 stability albeit with lower per-request quality.
- Notification: we can expose a webhook to your ops channel to notify of preemption/scale events in real time.

Commercial/operational asks:
- Mutual action plan (MAP): 2-week technical validation -> pilot month -> commit to quarterly reserved slab with an addendum for burst billing caps.
- Legal/procurement: sample addendum for burst capping and SLA exceptions included (see attached PDF).

Next steps:
1) Marcus to follow up with eviction/cooldown specifics and a short runbook.
2) Ben to propose a canary/observability checklist for the pilot.
3) Oliver — confirm acceptable cap on monthly burst spend (we can implement hard stop if you want).

Attaching: redwood_elastic_sizing_note.pdf (proposal + sample MAP)

Oliver — quick technical comments to complement Irene's proposal. Putting the ops guardrails here so your infra team can vet: 

1) Eviction & order-of-operations: when capacity is constrained we will (1) stop new burst allocations, (2) drain current burst-only requests, (3) preempt the lowest-priority burst nodes. We do not evict reserved slab GPUs. Preemption events will include a 30s drain window for in-flight token completions where possible.

2) Warm pools & cache pinning: for scheduled demos we recommend keeping a tiny warm pool (1–2 burst nodes) pinned 10 minutes before window to reduce cold-start variance. Additionally, we can pin the KV cache for the demo prompt sets to reserved slab so the warm pool boots with a primed cache.

3) Autoscale configuration suggestions:
   - Scale-up trigger: sustained 60s queue growth above 20% of reserved capacity.
   - Scale-down cooldown: 5 minutes after utilization drops below 40% for two consecutive windows.
   - Max concurrent scale actions: 2 (to avoid overprovisioning).

4) Model-fallback strategy: configure runtime to route to vicuna-7B automatically when burst pool is depleted; include a quality flag in responses so your app can decide whether to delay or surface degraded outputs.

5) Observability & alerts: we'll wire per-route p95/p99 and token burn dashboards; also expose preemption metrics + reason codes. Recommend a weekly post-mort during the pilot to tune headroom multipliers.

Adding a short ops checklist from the SRE side: 

- Canary week: route 10% of demo traffic through reserved+burst for 7 days; validate fallback quality and alerting.
- Preemption notifications: we can emit webhook + email; recommend a Slack webhook to your #infra-alerts for immediate visibility.
- Cost cap enforcement: two options — hard stop (block burst allocations after X spend) or soft cap (notify at 75%/90% and throttle). We recommend soft cap + hard stop for the first pilot month.
- Runbook stub: who to contact, escalation matrix, and a simple rollback to hosted API if Dedicated pilot has a major incident.

Irene — happy to run the canary runbook with your CS team. Oliver — what CP (cost param) do you want us to enforce during pilot?
